reply:
Still destructive. Force push replaces the branch tip on the remote with your new commit SHAs. The other developers have the old commits checked out locally, but `origin/branch` now points to different commits. On their next pull, git doesn't auto-merge—it detects a diverged history. They have to either `git reset --hard origin/branch` (losing local work), rebase their changes on top of yours, or manually untangle a conflicted state. The reflog keeps the old refs temporarily, but they're orphaned on the remote side.

The concrete cost: two people spend 30 minutes to an hour cleaning up a diverged branch instead of you telling them "rebase incoming" first.

`--force-with-lease` is safer (fails if the remote changed under you), but the real answer is a message: "I rebased. About to force-push—rebase or reset your local copy after."

grade.note: Reasserts destructiveness with mechanism (diverged refs, manual reset/rebase needed) and correctly notes reflog is local/orphaned remotely.
